name: Ranazjar Isle
summary: Ranazjar Isle is a rocky, storm-lashed outcrop lying just off the northwest coast of Desolace. Dotted with ancient night elven masonry, the island was until recently a stronghold for the serpentine naga before violence overtook their settlement.

sections.title: Ruins in the Shallows
sections.body: Ranazjar Isle sits west of the mainland cliffs, ringed by coastal waters and crumbling stone arches. The architecture scattered across the rocks belongs to the same ancient night elven city network as neighboring Ethel Rethor. For thousands of years, these drowned fragments remained quiet remnants of the Great Sundering, until the monstrous naga rose from the depths to claim the stone platforms for their own designs.

sections.title: The Naga's Ruin
sections.body: Though the Hatecrest naga carved out a commanding position here, their encampment met a sudden and brutal end. Travelers who swim or sail to the island find the naga settlement decimated, their bodies strewn across the weathered ruins. The slaughter was wrought by Lord Hydronis, an immense elemental entity whose wrath scourged the island's serpentine occupiers and left the isolated outcrop haunted by violence.

aliases: how to get to ranazjar isle
faq.answer: Ranazjar Isle is situated off the northwest shore of Desolace, in the waters directly west of the Ethel Rethor ruins.

faq.q: Who built the ruins on the island?
faq.answer: The stonework is ancient night elven architecture dating back prior to the Great Sundering. It is part of the same shattered metropolitan sprawl that forms the Ethel Rethor coastal ruins on the mainland.

faq.q: Why are all the naga dead on the island?
aliases: what killed the naga on ranazjar
faq.answer: The resident Hatecrest naga were slain and scattered across the rocks by the powerful water elemental known as Lord Hydronis, turning their outpost into an open-air graveyard.

faq.q: What is the connection between Ranazjar Isle and Ethel Rethor?
faq.answer: Both locations share the same architectural style, stonework, and age, suggesting that Ranazjar Isle was once a contiguous part or immediate harbor district of the ancient coastal elven complex before rising tides and cataclysm separated them.

angles.text: For the kaldorei, the desecrated masonry on Ranazjar Isle serves as a somber reminder of their ancient empire's coastal reaches, now defiled first by transformed brethren and then by rampaging elementals.
The utter destruction of the naga on the island stands as evidence of the unbridled fury of elemental spirits like Lord Hydronis when maritime boundaries are disturbed.
